title: Stillness and Movement Are Not Two
reflection: Once today, in a single breath, check that stillness and movement are one: where is the stillness in the movement of this breath?

questions.q: What does Conversation 1.4 say about stillness and movement?
o: Two faces of one whole: without movement, lifelessness; without stillness, agitation.
Two opposing forces, so that a person must pick one of them and then give up the other.
Two stages, so that a person must leave movement behind in order to reach stillness.
Two moods, so that a person has a good day whenever stillness wins out over movement.
questions.e: Remove movement and you get lifelessness; remove stillness and you get agitation without an anchor. You can check this in a single breath.
questions.c: Stillness and movement are one whole

questions.q: What picture does Conversation 1.4 use for the relationship?
o: An ocean and its waves: stillness is what it is, and waving is what it does.
A tree and its leaves: the leaves fall away, and the tree is left bare and still in winter.
A road and its travellers: the road stays where it is while the travellers come and go.
A clock and its hands: the face stands still while the hands go round and round it.
questions.e: Stillness is what the ocean is; waving is what it does. Nothing is added to or taken from the ocean when a wave rises.
questions.c: A wave is the ocean moving

questions.q: “A person who wants rest should remove all movement from their life.”
questions.e: Removing movement gives lifelessness. Genuine practice deepens engagement; it does not withdraw from life. Rest without guilt is possible because stillness is already present in the movement.
questions.c: Rest is found in movement, not by removing it

questions.q: A woman is exhausted and also restless, and cannot rest even when she stops. How does Conversation 1.4 read this?
o: Restlessness is the opposite of viśrānti: movement has lost its anchor in stillness.
Tiredness shows that she has done too little, so the answer is to take up much more activity.
Restlessness shows that she needs more silence, so the answer is to take herself away.
Tiredness and restlessness are unrelated, so each needs an unrelated and separate cure.
questions.e: Viśrānti is restful presence. Movement without a centre becomes agitation and burnout, and the cure is to restore the anchor, not to add more movement or flee from it.
questions.c: Restlessness is movement cut off from stillness

questions.q: A man says that his anxiety makes him feel like a wave with no ocean beneath. What does Conversation 1.4 suggest?
o: Anxiety is identification with the wave; the ocean is beneath, and returning to it steadies.
Anxiety proves that no ocean lies beneath, so there is nothing for him to return to there.
Anxiety is the ocean itself, so he must learn to be more at ease with the way it surges.
Anxiety is a fault of the waves, so he should try to flatten them all out by force of will.
questions.e: Anxiety is identification with the wave, with no sense of the ocean beneath. The teaching offers the return to the ground that is already there.
questions.c: Anxiety is identification with the wave alone

questions.q: A man uses the teaching “I am the still awareness” to avoid dealing with his problems. What does Conversation 1.4 say?
o: A true teaching misused as a hiding place: ground without life, and no refuge from living.
A true teaching rightly used: staying well clear of all problems is just what it is for.
A false teaching: still awareness is a fiction, so he should drop it and face his problems.
A harmless teaching: it has no effect, either on his problems or on the way he lives.
questions.e: The split is lived as suffering in this form too: ground without life. Genuine practice deepens engagement; it does not become a place to hide.
questions.c: Ground without life is a hiding place

questions.q: “Advaita Vedanta and Trika both point to presence in action, where Brahman and Śakti, or stillness and Spanda, are not two.”
questions.e: Advaita Vedanta speaks of Brahman and Śakti, and Trika of stillness and Spanda, the divine throb of movement. They meet in presence in action, which is the point of the lesson.
questions.c: The two contemplative traditions meet in presence in action

questions.q: A musician notices that each note arises from silence and returns to it. Which idea of Conversation 1.4 is this?
o: Movement arising from stillness and returning to it, like the ocean and its waves.
Silence as a lack of music, so that the two are opposed and cannot be heard together.
Silence as a rest between lessons, so that it is worth less than the notes themselves.
Notes as a disturbance of silence, so that a good musician plays as few of them as possible.
questions.e: Music and silence are an everyday picture of the one whole: the notes arise from silence and return to it, and the silence is what gives the notes their form.
questions.c: Notes arise from silence and return to it

questions.q: A doctor explains homeostasis to a patient. Which idea of Conversation 1.4 does it match?
o: Stability through movement: the body keeps steady by constantly adjusting, not by freezing.
Stability through rest: the body keeps steady by doing as little as it is able to do.
Instability as health: the body is well when its readings change as widely as they can.
Fixed readings: the body is well when every measure stays at one exact value all day.
questions.e: Biology shows stillness and movement as one: homeostasis is stability maintained through constant movement and correction.

questions.q: A man wants to try the experiment of Conversation 1.4 today. What does it ask?
o: In one breath, find the stillness inside the movement and the movement inside the stillness.
For one whole hour, keep entirely still, so as to find out what stillness is on its own.
For one whole hour, keep entirely busy, so as to find out what movement is on its own.
In one breath, decide which of the two he prefers and then practise that one alone.
questions.e: The check is made in a single breath: the breath moves, and there is a stillness in which it moves. They are two faces of one thing.
questions.c: Check the oneness in a single breath
